label: Wil McCarthy
narrative:
Wil McCarthy is the least conventional author in this batch and the one whose selection says the most about how AAWSAP sourced its expertise. He is an aerospace engineer and patent agent who began as a flight controller on Lockheed Martin space launch systems, moved to Omnitech Robotics as an engineering manager, served as chief technology officer of the aerospace research laboratory Galileo Shipyards, and is president of The Programmable Matter Corporation in Lakewood, Colorado. He is simultaneously a working science-fiction novelist, and it was in fiction that he first popularised the idea he was later paid by the Defense Intelligence Agency to survey. His "Queendom of Sol" novels, notably The Wellstone, are built around a substance he called wellstone: a programmable material whose effective atoms can be reconfigured on command so that a bounded but effectively unlimited range of material properties can be summoned or dismissed at will. He set the same idea out for a general readership in the non-fiction book Hacking Matter.

AAWSAP's statement of work included materials, structures and signature reduction. Programmable matter, quantum dots and reconfigurable metamaterial surfaces sit squarely in that space, and the pool of people who had written a book-length synthesis of the field in 2009 was tiny. McCarthy had both the engineering background to write to a defence-warning audience and a commercial vehicle, The Programmable Matter Corporation, through which the work could be contracted. His DIRD, "Aerospace Applications of Programmable Matter", is a twenty-page survey and carries the earliest publication date of the eight documents in this batch, 14 December 2009. He has no documented UAP-programme role beyond authorship of this single deliverable.
